lane: Identify the reflected UPROPERTY at +0x898 returned by the ULokiActorPoolManager pool gate (0x56363F0)
headline: The pool gate returns `ALokiGameState::bSupportsActorPoolPriming` — a plain EditDefaultsOnly `bool` at +0x898, NOT config-backed and NOT replicated — and the tutorial's own Blueprint class default sets it False (`Default__BP_LokiGameState_Tutorial_C.bSupportsActorPoolPriming = False`) while the C++ constructor sets it 1.
traps_hit: FOUR, all caught before they reached a conclusion. (1) HAND VA->RVA ARITHMETIC DROPPED A HEX DIGIT: 0x7FF7BB9C7100-0x7FF7B86D0000 computed by hand as 0x12F7100 instead of 0x32F7100; the wrong address disassembled to PLAUSIBLE code (`add edi,ebp; mov qword ptr [r14],rax`) rather than obvious garbage. Caught only by recomputing in python — exactly CLAUDE.md's "recompute with a machine" rule. (2) THE INSTRUMENT-ARTIFACT NEAR-MISS THAT WOULD HAVE MANUFACTURED A FALSE ABSENCE: my first FPropertyParams scan read `Offset` at +0x32 and returned FOUR hits at 0x898, none a bool — i.e. "there is no bool UPROPERTY at 0x898". FALSE: `FBoolPropertyParams` derives from `FPropertyParamsBase`, NOT `...WithOffset`, so +0x32 holds ElementSize and ALL 13,156 bool records read off=0x1. Caught by the impossible distribution (13,156/13,156 identical), not by suspicion. The real offset lives in a generated `SetBitFunc`. (3) My first EPropertyGenFlags table was off by two entries and labelled the known `CurrentPhase` enum as `LargeWorldCoordinatesReal`; caught by the calibration control, not by review. (4) `fkdis.py d <rva> n` takes n in BYTES, not instructions — `d 0x5676EF4 20` printed 2 instructions and read like the disassembler halting on undecodable bytes.

claims.claim: The gate's final read `movzx eax, byte ptr [rax + 0x898]` is at .text 0x05636438, bytes 0F B6 80 98 08 00 00 — no AND mask, so it returns the WHOLE byte.
claims.evidence: fkdis.py x 0x05636438 8 --dump s129 -> `0x05636438  0f b6 80 98 08 00 00 48`. fkdis.py cov 0x05636438 16 --dump s129 -> `page 0x05636000 present` (not coverage-blocked). fkdis.py d 0x56363F0 100 --dump s129 reproduces the whole gate including `0x05636438  0fb68098080000  movzx eax, byte ptr [rax + 0x898]`.

claims.claim: THE ANSWER: the reflected property at +0x898 is `bSupportsActorPoolPriming`, and it is the ONLY bool UPROPERTY at that offset in the entire image (13,156 Bool RECORDS swept; 0 coverage-blocked, 0 unrecognised).
claims.evidence: Wrote scratchpad/fk27/propscan.py (FPropertyParams decoder) + boolscan.py (SetBitFunc offset decoder). `python boolscan.py --dump s129 --stats --off 0x898` -> `Bool records: 13156 / mov 10310 / or 2791 / badptr 55` then `selected: 1` -> `0x08983A50 .rdata bSupportsActorPoolPriming off=0x1 dim=1 gen=Bool|NativeBool ... SetBitFunc=0x053800D0 [mov byte ptr [rcx + 0x898], 1] disp=0x898 mask=0x1 fold=1`. The 55 `badptr` all have SetBitFunc==NULL (container-inner / param bools with no outer object) — verified: `distinct raw pointer values: Counter({0: 55})` — so none can hide a candidate.

claims.claim: The SetBitFunc at .text 0x053800D0 is `mov byte ptr [rcx+0x898], 1; ret` (C6 81 98 08 00 00 01 C3), byte-identical in all three images, with fold multiplicity 1 — exactly ONE qword pointer to it image-wide, so it is uniquely identifying and not a shared fold.
claims.evidence: `fkdis.py x 0x053800D0 8` on s129 / merged2 / tuthero all -> `c6 81 98 08 00 00 01 c3`. Python scan of the whole image for the little-endian qword (0x053800D0+ImageBase): `qword pointers to SetBitFunc 0x053800D0 image-wide: 1`. `fkdis.py cov 0x053800D0 16 --dump s129` -> `page 0x05380000 present`.

claims.claim: CONTROL that the bool decoder is sound: `mov` vs `or` in SetBitFunc partitions EXACTLY on the 0x40 gen-flag bit — 2,791 `or` (bitfield bools) == 2,791 Bool records WITHOUT bit 0x40; 10,310 `mov` + 55 null == 10,365 records WITH it. Zero disagreement over 13,156 records.
claims.evidence: boolscan --stats: `mov 10310, or 2791, badptr 55`. Independent gen-flag census: `Bool hi=0x40 10365` of 13,156. 10310+55=10365 exactly; 13156-10365=2791 exactly. Worked bitfield examples: AActor::bAlwaysRelevant -> 0x032F7100 `or byte ptr [rcx+0x68], 8; ret`; AActor::bHidden -> 0x03368980 `or byte ptr [rcx+0x68], 0x80; ret`. Our target uses `mov ...,1` = whole-byte native bool, matching the maskless `movzx` read.
